full_judgment:
is directed an order dated 11.5.2004 passed by the learned Judge, Druto Bichar Tribunal No. l. Dhaka discharging the accused opposite party No.2 of the charge brought against his in Druto Bichar Tribunal Case No.4 of 2004 arising out of Shyampur Police Station CaseNo.12(7)2003 corresponding to G.R. No.2772 of 2003 under section 8/30 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain read with section 302/201/119 of the Penal Code, now pending for trial before the said Tribunal. 

 2. The facts of the case, briefly are that Md. Abdus Sultan, A.S.I. of Police Shyainpur P.S. D.M.P., Dhaka as informant lodged First Information Report (F.I.R.) at Shyampur P.S. on 8.7.2003 at 00.30 hours implicating Shoeb alias Shohel, the eldest son of the deceased landlord Solaiman alleging that on the night following 5.6.2003 at about 12.30 i.e. 6.7.2003 at 00.30 hours father of the victim Md. Saiful Islam, son of Korom A Ii Dhali, at present residing in the rented P.O. house at 787 south Dania known as Shahinder bari lodged written complaint regarding missing of his youngest son Tanjirul Islam alias Missel, aged 10 from the front gate of the house where he went on call of nature in the evening on 05.7.2003 at about 7.30 p.m. and since then could not be traced out. On receipt of the complaint Shyampur P.S. General diary No.270 dated 6.7.2003 was recorded upon interrogation of the father and mother of the victim and the witnesses surrounding the P.O. house by the informant during enquiry it revealed that even since the child was kidnapped unknown person called the father of the victim and demanded from him Taka three lacs as ransom for release of his kidnapped son over the telephone of his landlord in the house of Shohel alias Shoeb. In the body of the F.I.R. the names of three sons of the land lord Shohel alias Shoeb, Shahin and Yusuf are mentioned of whom involvement of accused Shoeb alias Shohel, son of deceased landlord Solaiman with the kidnapping the victim child prima-facie made revealed. It further revealed that at the time of occurrence accused Shoeb talked over mobile phone standing in front of the gate of the P.O. house and he had a motor cycle with him. At that point of time the victim became untraceable. On request by police the father and mother of the victim refused to file a case out of fear. Hence said A.S.I. Md. Abdus Sultan, had to file a belated case. On receipt of the F.I.R. Shyampur P.S. Case No.12 dated 8.7.2003 under section 8 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain was started. Mr. Anwar Hossain, S.I. of Police, Shyampur Police Station took up the investigation. 

 3. On 14.7.2003 Saiful Islam father of the victim filed a petition being Petition No.I888 of 2003 in the court of the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka implicating 8 accused person alleging, direct involvement of accused Shoeb alias Shohel and his three brothers Md. Shahin, Md. Suman and Md. Yusuf, Mrs. Latifa Begum wife of Md. Shahin, Mrs. Shirin Akter Jali, Mrs. Mali wife of Md. Suman and Md. Hanif alleging inter alia that after the occurrence the accused persons had been absconding with the victim and as the thana Police failed to lake steps for recovery of the victim the investigation of the case should be conducted C.I.D. of Police. 

 6. Pursuant to the decision of the monitoring cell in the Ministry of Home Affairs for speedy disposal of important cases of grave offences Mr. Md. Khalequzzaman, A.S.P. of CID Special Team took up the investigation of the case further examined P.Ws., mother, brother and some relations of the victim and interrogated some police 'personnel of Shyampur P.S. and recorded their statements under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and also seized alamats of the case namely 1) the original copies of 1) General diary No.270 dated 6.7.2003 bearing endorsement of the officer-in-charge Shyampur Police Station on 6.7.2003 to S.I. Abdus Sukur and A.S.I. Abdus Sultan respectively for taking necessary action, 2) application for bail dated 7.7.2003 addressed to the officer-in-charge Shyampur P.S. 3) General diary 382 and 394 dated 7.7.2004 recorded by Anwar Hossain, S.I. of Police and the officer-in-charge in connection with arrest and detention of accused Shahin at thana hajat and release of accused Shahin on bail No.4) Daily duty roster of S.I. and A.S.I. of police of Shyampur P.S. for the month of July, 2003 and 5) M.C.C. No.1761 of 2003 dated 7.7.2003 at time 10.50 hours issued for deployment of Md. Abdus Sultan along with 3 constable under the direction of D.C. (East) D.M.P. at different places of Shyampur P.S. for search and recovery of victim Tanjirul Islam alias Missel in connection with G.D. No.270 dated 6.7.2003. Thereafter the officer of the Special team of C.I.D. on conclusion of the investigation submitted charge sheet against. 5 accused persons under relevant sections of the Nari-O-Shishu .Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2003 read with various Sections of the Penal Code, for prosecution including the accused officer-in-charge Zahangir Alam (accused opposite party No.2 herein) hereinafter called the accused officer-in-Charge under section 8/30 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain. 2000 read with section 302/201/119 with the recommendation for release of another 6 accused persons from the case. 

 7. The case was sent to the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjata n Tribunal No.1 for trial. On receipt of the case record by the said Tribunal the case was registered as Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal case No.47 of 2004 and the Tribunal by order dated 25.1.2004 took cognizance of the offences involving all the accused person's sent up in the charge sheet. Subsequently the Government in the Ministry of Home Affairs by gazette notification dated 29.4.2004 transferred the case to Druto Bichar Tribunal, Dhaka for speedy disposal of the case. On receipt of the case record by the Druto Bichar Tribunal from the file of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Dhaka it was registered and numbered as Druto Bichar Tribunal Case No.4 of 2004 before the said Tribunal. 

 8. Thereafter accused ex-officer-in-Charge moved the High Court Division with an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure with prayer for quashing the proceeding of the aforesaid Tribunal Case against the accused petitioner contending inter alia that the accused petitioner is innocent and committed no offence and that there is no foundation of the charge that lie facilitated the brought, against. him that accused persons in kidnapping the victim or assisted the accused persons in killing the victim and concealing the dead body which is prima-facie unwarranted and not sustainable and as such continuance of the trial against the accused is an abuse of the process of the court and liable to be quashed for the ends of justice. 

 10. On 6.5.2004 accused ex-officer-in-charge moved the Druto Bichar Tribunal with an application under section 24IA of the Code of Criminal Procedure with prayer to discharge him from the charge brought against him. The Tribunal by judgment and order dated 11.5.2004 allowed the application moved in suppression of the fact that on similar contentions the High Court Division refused to quash the proceeding of Tribunal Case No.4 of 2004 against the accused officer-in-charge. 

 11. It appears from the record of the Tribunal that the judgment and order dated 13.4.2004 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3202 of 2004 refusing to quash the proceeding tinder section 561-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure was received by the Druto Bichar Tribunal on 27.06.2004. In the meantime Druto Bichar Tribunal discharged the accused petitioner by order dated 11.5.2005 framed charge the rest 4 charge sheeted accused persons to which they pleaded innocence and claimed trial, closed the entire evidence of P.Ws. examined said accused persons under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure who again pleaded not guilty and declined to adduce any D.W.; heard argument and fixed the next date on 30.7.2004 for delivery of judgment. Hence the Suo Moto Rule. 

 12. The accused ex-officer-in-charge, being the accused petitioner in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3202 of 2004 entered appearance and contested the Rule by filing counter-affidavit in support of the averments in the petition filed before the Tribunal for discharge, contending inter alia that Druto Bichar Tribunal No.1, Dhaka discharged the accused opposite party No.2 justly and properly because he is not named not even suspected in the F.I.R. and in the petition of complainant filed by the father of the victim before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. The said accused has not been implicated in any manner with the occurrence, in the confessional statement made by accused Momtaz Mal alias Jamai Momtaj before the Magistrate on 26.7.2003 and none of the P.Ws. in their statements recorded under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure implicated the accused officer-in-Charge with the offence. The charge is absolutely groundless and untenable. 

 13. At the time of hearing of the Rule we sought assistance of Mr. Khondakar Mahbub Hossain, senior advocate as a amicus curiae and Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, advocate to assist him to determine as to whether belated interference by the High Court Division in the instant case fixed for judgment will be justified the learned advocates agreed and offered their valuable assistance. Mr. Mahbub Hoassain, the learned Senior advocate submits that the High Court Division is competent to interfere and set aside any order and issue any direction upon a court of Tribunal Sub-ordinate to it in exercise of it inherent power under section 561-A of the Code of criminal Procedure to prevent the abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice even after delivery of judgment in the case. There is no limit to such power. The learned advocate further submits that the settled principle of law is that the extent and scope of such interference lies it the discretion of the court on consideration of the facts and circumstances in each case. Mr. Munsurul Haque Chowdhury, the learned advocate appearing for the discharged ex-Officer-in-Charge concedes to this proposition of law placed by the learned amicus curiae. Section 7 of the Druto Bichar Tribunal provides that a Tribunal constituted under the Ain will be treated as Sessions court and procedure for trial in Chapter XX of the Code of Criminal Procedure applies. We are in agreement with this contention of Mr. Khandaker Mahbub Hossain, learned advocate. 

 14. Mr. Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned advocate appearing from the bar vigorously submits that the High Court Division in rejecting the prayer for quashing the case against the accused opposite party in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3202 of 2004 made specific finding and observation that on consideration of the facts and circumstances and materials on record there are direct and specific allegations as to the involvement of the accused petitioner (discharged accused) in suppressing the conspiracy to commit to commit the offence of kidnapping the child Missel for collection money in ransom murder and concealment of the dead body. It is further held by the High Court Division that whether the discharged accused officer-in-charge suppressed the design or conspiracy it’s alleged or not is to be determined on consideration of evidence to be adduced at the time of trial. The learned advocate continued to submit that the above finding decision of the High Court Division is binding upon the Druto Bichar Tribunal and as such the subsequent order of discharge of the accused opposite party obtained from the Tribunal in fraudulent suppression of the order dated 13.4.2004 passed by the High Court Division is prima-facie without jurisdiction and liable to be set aside. Mr. Khan then submits the allegation against the discharged Officer-in-Charge that he suppressed the conspiracy to commit the offence of kidnapping and subsequent murder of the child Missel and concealment of the dead body is revealed from the G.Ds. seized as alamats and the statements of the P.Ws. namely Saiful Islam, the father, Firoza Begum, mother and police officials namely Abdus Sukur, S.I. of Police and Md. Abdus Sultan, A.S.I. of police and prima-facie case having been made out against the accused officer-in-charge the special officer, C.I.D. and the I.O submitted the charge sheet against him under section 8/30 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 read with section 302/201/119 of the Penal Code. 

 15. Perused the Shyampur P.S. General diary No.270 dated 6.7.2003 about missing of victim child Tanjirul Islam alias Missel recorded on written complaint lodged by Saiful Islam, father of victim, G. Ds. No.382, 392 and 394 dated 7.7.2003 recorded by Anwar Hossain, S.I. Police, Md. Abdus Sultan, A.S.I. and Md. Zahangir A lam, officer-in-charge respectively of Shyampur P.S. Case No.12 dated. 8.7.2003 lodged Suo Moto by Md. Abdus Sultan, A.S.I. of Police statement of witnesses recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C., application under section 241A Cr. P. C. filed by accused Officer-in-Charge praying for discharging him from the charge brought against him and the judgment and order dated 11.5.2004 passed by the Tribunal discharging the accused officer-in-charge Md. Zahangir Alam, carefully and heard Mr. Munsurul Haque Chowdhury, the learned advocate appearing for the accused opposite party No.2 and the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the state at length. The learned advocate appearing for the accused Officer-in-Charge taking us through the relevant G.Ds. seized as alamats, F.I.R. statement of the witnesses and confessional statement of accused Momtaz Mal alias Jamai Momtaz emphatically submits that the accused-opposite-party innocent and committed no offence and he has been falsely implicated in the charge sheet for an offence under section 8/30 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 read with section 302/201/119of the Penal Code which is not only groundless but also malicious and as such not sustainable. 

 16. From the F.I.R. and other materials on record it is revealed that place of occurrence is the ground floor of the two storied house of accused Shahin and Shoeb at 787, Dania and their family members where Saiful Islam, father of the victim along with family including child Missel resided as tenant and from gate of the house Missel was kidnapped on 5.7.2003 at 7.30 p.m. The father of victim who is a vital prosecution witness and lodged the complaint of G.D. No.270 in his statement to the I.O. narrated that they suspected Shoeb and his brother Shahin to have kidnapped his son and it is none but accused Shoeb who by changing his voice demanded taka three lacs for release of his son with threat to kill him unless the demand was fulfilled over the own telephone of accused Shoeb in the house of land lord at about 10.30 P.M. On return of Shoeb at about 12.00 hours at night when he was told by the witness (father) that he (Shoeb) had taken his son and demanded return of victim to him Shoeb flatly denied his involvement with the occurrence and at this stage aforesaid accused took him to thana in his motor cycle and got manipulated General Diary (G.D. No.270) about simple missing of his son recorded in his name. P.W. Feroza Begum mother and P.W. Shafiqul Islam the brother of the victim who are eye witnesses in their statement to the I. O. supported the father P.W. Saiful [slam in material particulars. In G.D. No.392 lodged by A.S.I. Md. Abdus Sultan stated that it was not an incident of mere missing but kidnapping the child for realising ransom which is prima-facie proved during inquiry. It is also revealed that at the time of occurrence Shoeb talked with mobile phone standing at the gate and had motor cycle with him; that father and mother were terrified for which they refused to lodged F.I.R. out of fear. The father of the victim also stated to I.O. that he was informed by accused Shahin that he held talk with unknown person who claimed taka One lac for release of the victim. At this the family members of the victim became scared of their security and abandoned the rented house and shifted to the house of Abdur Rahman the brother-in-law of P.W. Saiful Islam the father of the victim. S.I. Abdus Sukur another prosecution witness stated to the 1.0 . that while on emergency duty from 19.45 hours on 6.7.2003 up to 8.00 a.m. of the morning of 7.7.2003 at about 12.30 a.m. at night of 7.7.2003 he was called by the accused officer-in-charge at thana and was directed to took into the G.D. matter by putting back dated endorsement on 6.7.2003 but the original of the Diary had been retained by the accused officer-in-charge purposely. Again the accused ex-officer-in-charge made similar endorsement on the body of the G.D. No.270 in the name of A.S.I. Sultan showing back date of 6.7.2003 but held the original G.D. in his control and possession without letting him to know anything about the matter immediately. It is stated that on 7.7.2003 at 14.45 hours the endorsee A.S.I. Md. Sultan along with 3(three) constable issued command certificate for search and recovery of the victim vide Shyampur P.S. M.C.C. No.1761 and he was supplied a photo copy of G.D. No.270 dated 6.7.2003. From the G.D. No.392 dated 7.7.2003 recorded by A.S.I. Abdus Sultan and his statement recorded under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure it is evident that upon interrogation of the parents and the local witnesses from the surrounding area they suspected and pointed their finger to accused Shoeb locally known for his notoriety who in collusion with his accomplices, with evil design to commit wrongful gain kidnapped the child Missel and kept in hide out and demanded the amount in ransom for release of his son over his own telephone. A.S.I. Abdus Sultan got definite clue that it is not a case of simple missing of the child from the gate but kidnapping the victim child. 

 17. P.W. Anwar Hossain, A.S.I. Shyampur P.S. who is the first Investigation Officer (I.O) stated that he had gone to visit the place of occurrence and on the basis of materials provided by the parents of the victim and information received from the local witnesses arrested accused Shahin whose complicity in the occurrence transpired and detained him at thana hajat on 7.7.2003 at 20.10 hours with a view to seeking remand of the accused in custody for interrogation. Under G.D. Entry No.382 dated 7.7.2003 under Section 54 of Cr. P.C. But the accused officer-in-charge released him on bail from thana lock up within one hour forty minutes of his arrest at 21.50 hours before lodging the F.I.R. without providing any opportunity to the arresting Officer to interrogate the accused regarding his involvement. Frorri the statement of S.I. Abdul Awal it appears under the order of the accused officer-in-charge on 7.7.2003 at about 21.00 hours he obtained signature of Saiful Islam the father of the victim. Firoza Begum, the mother and Shafiqul Islam the brother of the victim on the margin of the blank sheet below the names and address of 4(four) unnamed persons including the father-in-law of accused Shahin and got G.D. Entry No.394 dated 7.7.2003 and plain sheet of paper filled up by P.W. A.S.I. Sajjad Hossain a5 an application for bail and also undertaking of the parents of the victim not to file any case against Shoeb and others accused persons in connection with above incident as dictated by the accused officer-in-charge. 

 18. From the above it appears that accused Shoeb and his three accomplices are involved in kidnapping the victim child Misse I for ransom and gruesome murder of the victim child by Shoeb with his two accomplices by throttle and after killing cutting at the neck of the victim to separate it and concealment of the dead body between 7.30 p.m. to 3 p.m. at the fateful night following 5.7.2003. On realization of shrewed Shoeb that after the institution of G.D. Complaint 270 dated 6.7.2003 father and mother of the victim and other P.W s. already had definite and firm view that deceased Shoeb and his cohorts was behind the occurrence and threat and pressure to kill the victim to make monetary gain ended in failure. From the statements of P.Ws. oral and circumstantial on record show that the fact of involvement of Shoeb and his accomplices in kidnapping the victim child and his confinement in unknown hide out revealed in the locality immediately after the occurrence and was talked out publicly. The accused Officer-in-Charge being duty bound to prevent commission of offence on receipt of written complaint from the father regarding missing child on which General Diary No.270 dated 6.7.2003 was instituted at 00.40 hours by willful negligence to his duty and making illegal omission for illegal and immoral purpose took no step regarding recovery of the victim child and thereby facilitated the accused persons in the killing and concealment of the dead body after kidnapping an innocent child like Missel. Further more the accused being the officer-in-Charge of the Police Station by taking no initiative on receipt of complaint about commission of such heinous offence assisted the main accused and his accomplices by suppressing their conspiracy. The belated endorsement of the G.D. to S.I. Sukur and A.S.I. Abdus Sultan after lapse of twenty four hours is intentional and provided opportunity to accused Shoeb and which would go to show that the accused Officer-in-Charge had prior connivance with other accused as alleged in the charge sheet. From our scrutiny we find material evidence of instances of acts and illegal suppression and omission on the part of the accused Officer-in-Charge available on record. It is true that validity of each particular actor suppression or omission attributed to the accused officer is to be decided on consideration of evidence adduced at the time of trial of the case. 

 20. The Druto Bichar Tribunal No.1 itself passed an order dated 27.6.2004 and observed that the Tribunal received not -information about the judgment passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3202 of 2004. It further held that neither accused opposite party mentioned in the petition filed under section 241 Cr. P.C. nor his engaged lawyer furnished the information or placed the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in the aforesaid Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3202 of 2004 on record. As such the tribunal after passing the order of discharge of the accused officer-in-charge had no any kind of jurisdiction to pass any further order against him. 

 It may be noted that the finding and decision of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3202 of 2004 has not been challenged by the accused Officer-in-Charge before the Appellate Division. 

 22. There are evidence on record to show the accused officer-in-charge had definite knowledge about the occurrence and only after Shoeb and his accomplices killed the victim child after kidnapping him within couple of hours at the night following 5.7.2003 the accused officer-in-charge made back dated endorsement of G.D. No. 270 purportedly on 6.7.2003 in the name of S.I. Abdus Sukur and A.S.I. Abdus Sultan for enquiry and necessary action as mentioned above. On the face of specific allegation of connivance of the accused Officer-in-Charge with the accused and suppression of conspiracy to commit the offence against him supported by material on record the: excuse put forward by the accused officer in charge that Shyampur P.S. is crime riddled station and O.C.s in the Metropolitan area remains pre-occupied with multifarious matters of law an order. As such little delay in making over the G.D. Entry to his subordinate officer for enquiry is not unusual; that accused officer in charge over all supervised the case leading to successful investigation by way of recovery of the dead body do not provide any ground for discharge and are not at all tenable. 

 Moreover the according to the finding of the Tribunal itself impugned order for discharge of the accused Officer-in-Charge obtained from the Tribunal fraudulently by suppressng the finding and decision of the High Court Division dated 13.4.2004 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3202 of 2004 is prima facie unlawful, an abuse of the process of the court and not sustainable. 

 26. The order dated 11.5.2004 passed by the Druto Bichar Tribunal No.1, Dhaka discharging the accused officer-in-charge opposite party No.2 from the Charge brought against him in Tribunal Case No.4 of 2004 is set aside. The specified time limit of 135 days for conclusion the Trial having already expired in the meantime this case must be returned to the concerned Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal for disposal in accordance with law. 

 27. The lower Court records be sent down to the Druto Bichar Tribunal No.1 with direction to send the case records of Nari-O-Shishu Nidatan Daman Tribunal  Case No.47/2004 arising out of Shyampur P.S. Case No.12 dated 5.7.2003, corresponding to G.R. No.2772/2003 to Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal No.1, Dhaka. The concerned Tribunal is directed to frame charge against charge sheet .SL.5 accused Md. Zahangir Alam, son of Md. Abdul Hakim, ex-Officer-in-Charge, Shyampur Police Station D.M.P. Dhaka under Section 8/30 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 read with Section 302/201/119 of the Penal Code and try him according to the provision of Section 229-231 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and on completion of the trial pronounce the judgment on respective charge brought against  each accused including the said accused Md. Zahangir Alam, ex-Officer-in-Charge. 

 28. The order of stay all further proceedings of Druto Bichar Tribunal Case No.4 of 2004 stands vacated.
